I am a Research Assistant Professor in the Department of Mathematics at Dartmouth College.

I research complex and physical systems using a plethora of tools, including data-driven and
operator-theoretic methods for understanding and predicting complex nonlinear systems, with
applications ranging from weather and climate to plasma physics and neuroscience. I work with
collaborators in mathematics, physics, computer science, engineering and domain sciences.

I got my degrees at the Faculty of Physics of the University of Warsaw. I took my M.S. in Physics
with Honors in 2005, at the Astronomical Observatory, working in astrophysics on asteroseismology
under Wojciech A. Dziembowski; that work led to a study of the regular pulsation of two luminous
blue variable stars in NGC 300. I stayed in Warsaw for my Ph.D., taken in 2011 at the Institute of
Geophysics in computational geophysics and fluid dynamics, with a dissertation on the impact of
entrainment and mixing on the optical properties of shallow cumulus clouds. Throughout those years I
spent roughly half of each year at the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) in Boulder,
Colorado, where my mentor was Dr. Wojciech W. Grabowski, a senior researcher there. In 2025 I
completed a Postgraduate Diploma in Management at the SGH Warsaw School of Economics, with a thesis
on evolutionary ownership and machine learning of strategy.

Before Dartmouth, I was a postdoctoral associate at the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences at
NYU and at the Center for Prototype Climate Modeling at NYU Abu Dhabi, a research associate in the
Department of Physics at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee, and a senior researcher at the
Finnish Center for Artificial Intelligence and the Department of Computer Science of the University
of Helsinki. I joined Dartmouth in 2022.
